newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-SOWETO TEAM FACES HUMILIATING DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOWETO TEAM FACES HUMILIATING DEFEAT.

text.p: South Africa's Orlando Pirates, who threatened to create a new era in African club soccer just over a year ago, face humiliating defeat in the first round of the African Champions Cup on the weekend.
The much-beloved Soweto club, known in South Africa as the "people's team", broke a 12-year stranglehold by clubs from Arab-speaking north Africa when they won the top African club title in 1995.
It was the first time since 1983 that a team from sub-Saharan Africa had taken the Champions Cup and signaled a change in African soccer's powerbase.

Last year Pirates lost in a penalty shootout at the quarter-final stage in defence of their title but were among the favourites to again bid for the Champions Cup this year -- and strike another blow for club soccer in the southern region.
But now the Buccaneers face defeat in the first round of the competition at the hands of Roma Rovers, a student team from the tiny mountain kingdom of Lesotho.
Pirates have a slender 1-0 lead to take to Maseru for Sunday's second leg and will face a fanatical country bent on upsetting the star attraction from their powerful neighbouring country.
The match has top billing among all the African club competition first round, first leg games this weekend.

Rovers, playing in the Champions Cup for the first time, scored five goals at home in the preliminary round and will be better placed to used the uneven bounce and difficult conditions of the Sesotho stadium in Maseru.
Added in their favour is the fact that Pirates remain rudderless after coach Augusto Palacios was attacked by angry fans earlier this month after Pirates lost a league match.
Rovers are not the only minnows with a chance of a rare upset this weekend.

Notwane from Botswana are in line to reach the second round for the first time in club history when they host Primiero de Agosto of Angola in Gaborone on Sunday after scoring a 1-1 draw away in Luanda in the first leg two weeks ago.

In the African Cup Winners' Cup, Senegalese second division club US Goreenne take a 1-0 lead to Algeria for their second leg tie against Mouloudia Oran while Confederation of African Football (CAF) Cup holders Kawkab Marrakesh travel to Senegal with aslender one-goal lead against ASC la Linguere.
Kawkab, who became the first Moroccan team to win the CAF Cup last year, needed a second-half penalty to win the game.
